unit.label: Visit plans, conditions & fruit
unit.title: If You Come to Visit
unit.description: Finish visit dates and conditions, then transition into fruit language through one continuing visit-and-hosting context.

goal.text: 要是你來，我就給你一塊水果。
goal.pinyin: Yàoshi nǐ lái, wǒ jiù gěi nǐ yí kuài shuǐguǒ.
goal.meaning: If you come, I’ll give you a piece of fruit.

unit.bookReference: A Course in Contemporary Chinese 1 · Lesson 9 Dialogue II / Vocabulary II and Grammar I/V (printed pp. 185–193), then Lesson 10 Dialogue I / Vocabulary I opening material (printed pp. 202–204). This pass restores the source-listed 女 + noun pattern and 逛, then continues with 水果, 黃色, 給, 香, 甜 and 以前. Existing published step IDs and positions remain stable.

lessons.title: A Visit Date — and What to Eat
lessons.subtitle: Say when someone is coming, then carry that visit naturally into the first this lesson word 水果.

steps.prompt: Which spoken date means September 30?
steps.explanation: 九月 is September and 三十號 is the 30th.

steps.prompt: Which marker is common in a spoken day-of-month date?
steps.explanation: 號 follows the day number in spoken dates.

steps.prompt: Which word means “fruit”?
steps.explanation: 水果 is the general word for fruit.

lessons.title: What Else Is There?
lessons.subtitle: Use 還 to add something, then describe the added fruit by color.

steps.prompt: In 我還不知道, what does 還 mean?
steps.explanation: The state of not knowing continues: still do not know.

steps.prompt: In 這裡還有茶館, what does 還 add?
steps.explanation: 還有 adds something else that is present.

steps.prompt: Which word means the color yellow?
steps.explanation: 黃色 is yellow; 色 means color.

lessons.title: At Maokong, Share a Piece
lessons.subtitle: Keep the Maokong visit context and use 給 naturally while sharing food.

steps.prompt: Which Taipei place is associated here with tea and scenery?
steps.explanation: 貓空 is the Taipei destination associated here with tea and scenery.
貓 is māo, the first character of 貓空.

steps.prompt: Which verb means “to give”?
steps.explanation: 給 is the verb “to give.”

lessons.title: If It Smells Good, I’ll Eat It
lessons.subtitle: Use 要是…就… with 香 so the condition and the new food description reinforce each other.

steps.prompt: Which word introduces the consequence in 要是…就…?
steps.explanation: 要是 marks the condition; 就 begins the consequence predicate.

steps.prompt: Which sentence uses the taught 要是…就… frame to mean “If I am free, then I will go with you”?
options: 要是我有空，我就跟你一起去。
我有空，所以跟你一起去。
你要是有空，你就跟我一起去。
steps.answer: 要是我有空，我就跟你一起去。
steps.explanation: The first option keeps the intended subject and uses 要是 for the condition and 就 for its consequence.

steps.prompt: Which word describes a pleasant smell?
steps.explanation: 香 means fragrant or good-smelling.

lessons.title: If It Isn’t Sweet
lessons.subtitle: Keep the negative condition-consequence pattern and use 甜 inside the condition.

steps.prompt: Which sentence correctly uses a negative condition and a negative consequence?
options: 你要是沒空，我們就不去夜市。
你要是有空，我們就去夜市。
steps.answer: 你要是沒空，我們就不去夜市。
steps.explanation: 沒空 is the negative condition; 就不去夜市 is the negative consequence.

steps.prompt: Can the subject come before 要是?
options: Yes, as in 你要是沒空…
No, 要是 must always be the first word
steps.answer: Yes, as in 你要是沒空…
steps.explanation: this lesson explicitly allows 要是 before or after the subject of the condition clause.

steps.prompt: Which word describes a sweet taste?
steps.explanation: 甜 means sweet in taste.

lessons.title: Earlier Preferences, Today’s Visit
lessons.subtitle: Use 以前 in a familiar preference frame while recycling the fruit vocabulary from this unit.

steps.prompt: Your plan depends on whether you are free. Which frame expresses that dependency?
steps.explanation: 要是…就… presents a condition and its consequence.

steps.prompt: Which date expression belongs before the action as a Time-When phrase?
steps.explanation: A calendar date answers when; the other two answer how long.

steps.prompt: Which word means “before; in the past”?
steps.explanation: 以前 refers to an earlier time or the past.

lessons.title: Unit 29 Review
lessons.subtitle: Dates, conditions, and the first fruit-description vocabulary from this lesson.

steps.explanation: 月 is yuè, month.
水 is shuǐ, the first character of 水果.
給 is gěi, to give.

steps.prompt: Which spoken date means October 13?
steps.explanation: Month comes first: 十月 is October, 十三號 is the 13th.

steps.prompt: In 我還不知道, 還 means:
steps.explanation: The state continues.

steps.prompt: In 這裡還有茶館, 還 means:
steps.explanation: 還有 adds another item.

steps.prompt: Which verb means “to wander around / look around,” as in 去逛逛?
steps.explanation: 逛 means to wander or look around; 去逛逛 describes a casual visit.

steps.prompt: Which word marks the condition?
steps.explanation: 要是 introduces the if-clause.

steps.prompt: Which word marks the consequence?
steps.explanation: 就 introduces the result predicate.

steps.prompt: Which sentence means “If she is free, we will go to Maokong”?
options: 她要是有空，我們就去貓空。
她要是沒空，我們就去貓空。
她要是有空，我們就不去貓空。
steps.answer: 她要是有空，我們就去貓空。
steps.explanation: 她 precedes 要是; 有空 is the positive condition and 就去貓空 is the consequence.

steps.prompt: Which component is on the left of 給?
steps.explanation: 給 has 糹 on the left and 合 on the right.

steps.prompt: Which sentence means “I return to my country on September 30”?
steps.explanation: The correct sentence keeps both the date 九月三十號 and the action 回國.

steps.prompt: If the condition is negative, does 就 disappear?
options: No, 就 still introduces the consequence
Yes, replace 就 with 還 after a negative condition
Yes, 就 is only used after affirmative conditions
steps.answer: No, 就 still introduces the consequence
steps.explanation: The condition can be negative without changing the 要是…就… frame.

steps.prompt: In this lesson the vocabulary set, what does 女 do in 女學生?
options: Means the person is a friend
steps.explanation: 女 + person noun works as female-/girl-, for example 女學生. This is distinct from simply memorizing the fixed word 女朋友.

steps.prompt: Which sentence means “In the past, I didn’t like eating yellow fruit”?
options: 我以前不喜歡吃黃色的水果。
我以前很喜歡吃黃色的水果。
我現在不喜歡吃黃色的水果。
steps.answer: 我以前不喜歡吃黃色的水果。
steps.explanation: 以前 sets the time in the past, 不喜歡 gives the negative preference, and 黃色的 modifies 水果.

steps.prompt: Which sentence pair means “I give you a piece of fruit. The fruit smells fragrant and tastes sweet”?
options: 我給你一塊水果。水果很香，也很甜。
我帶你去吃水果。水果很香，也很甜。
我給你一塊水果。水果很特別，但是不甜。
steps.answer: 我給你一塊水果。水果很香，也很甜。
steps.explanation: 給 means give; 香 describes a pleasant smell; 甜 describes a sweet taste.

newVocabulary.meaning: date; numbered day of a month

newVocabulary.note: The character was seen earlier in 還是; this is the first formal teaching of 還 as an independent adverb.

newVocabulary.meaning: Maokong, a Taipei place known for tea and scenery

newVocabulary.note: The character was introduced earlier in 甜點; this is its first standalone vocabulary teaching.
this lesson the vocabulary set gives 女 + noun as a productive person label, for example 女學生.
去逛逛 describes casually going to look around a night market.

月.note: 月 is fourth-tone yuè. After a number, it names a month, as in 九月.
月.memory: The first two strokes make the tall outer shape; the final two short horizontals sit inside it.

parts.name: outer frame
parts.description: The first two strokes form the tall outer frame of 月.

parts.label: 二
parts.name: inner lines
parts.description: The last two strokes are the two short horizontal lines inside.

號.note: 號 is fourth-tone hào. After a number in a date, it means the numbered day of the month.
號.memory: A compact five-stroke left sound component balances the eight-stroke 虎 component on the right.

parts.label: 号
parts.name: left sound component
parts.description: The first five strokes form the compact left component with 口 above a hooked lower shape.

parts.label: 虎
parts.name: tiger component
parts.description: The final eight strokes form 虎 on the right.

就.note: 就 is fourth-tone jiù. In 要是…就…, it introduces the consequence of the condition.
就.memory: 京 fills the left eight strokes; 尤 completes the right with four strokes.

parts.label: 京
parts.name: left component
parts.description: The first eight strokes form 京 on the left.

parts.label: 尤
parts.name: right component
parts.description: The final four strokes form 尤 on the right.

example.pinyin: Yàoshi yǒu kòng, jiù yìqǐ qù.
example.meaning: If there is time, then go together.

貓.meaning: cat; first character of 貓空
貓.note: 貓 is first-tone māo. Here it is learned as the first character of the Taipei place name 貓空.
貓.memory: 豸 uses the first seven strokes on the left; 苗 uses the final nine strokes on the right.

parts.label: 豸
parts.name: left component
parts.description: The first seven strokes form 豸 on the left.

parts.label: 苗
parts.name: right component
parts.description: The final nine strokes form 苗 on the right, with 艹 above 田.

水.meaning: water; first character of 水果
水.note: 水 is third-tone shuǐ. In 水果, the word as a whole means fruit.
水.memory: 水 is a basic four-stroke radical form. Its central vertical hook anchors the two flowing side strokes, so it is best learned as one whole shape.

parts.label: 水
parts.name: water radical
parts.description: All four strokes form the independent water radical 水; forcing it into borrowed components would be less useful than learning its balanced whole shape.

果.note: 果 is third-tone guǒ. In 水果, it supplies the fruit meaning directly.
果.memory: Write a four-stroke 日-shaped box first. The following 木-shaped group sends its vertical through that box, creating the final 田-like appearance.

parts.label: 日-shaped box
parts.name: upper box
parts.description: The first four strokes form a 日-shaped box, not a complete five-stroke 田. The vertical through its center comes later with the 木-shaped group.

parts.label: 木
parts.name: tree component
parts.description: The last four strokes form the 木-shaped lower portion that passes through the center of the character.

果.partOrderLabel: 田 first, then the 木-shaped lower strokes

黃.note: 黃 is second-tone huáng and is the color word yellow.
黃.memory: The four-stroke top sits above a broad middle and the final 八-like two strokes at the bottom.

parts.label: 廿
parts.name: top component
parts.description: The first four strokes form the compact 廿-like top of 黃.

parts.label: 一 + 田 + 八
parts.name: lower body
parts.description: After the four-stroke top, write the long horizontal, the five-stroke 田-like middle, and the two separate lower strokes.

色.note: 色 is fourth-tone sè. After a color word such as 黃, it forms 黃色, “yellow.”
色.memory: Two short ⺈ strokes sit above the four-stroke 巴 shape.

parts.name: top component
parts.description: The first two strokes form the small ⺈ shape at the top.

parts.label: 巴
parts.name: bottom component
parts.description: The final four strokes form 巴 underneath.

給.note: 給 is third-tone gěi. In this lesson it is the verb “to give.”
給.memory: 糹 takes six strokes on the left; 合 takes six on the right.

parts.label: 糹
parts.name: silk component
parts.description: The first six strokes form 糹 on the left.

parts.label: 合
parts.name: right component
parts.description: The final six strokes form 合 on the right.

香.note: 香 is first-tone xiāng. For food, it describes a pleasant smell.
香.memory: 禾 forms the five-stroke top; 日 forms the four-stroke bottom.

parts.label: 禾
parts.name: grain component
parts.description: The first five strokes form 禾 at the top.

parts.label: 日
parts.name: sun component
parts.description: The final four strokes form 日 below.

逛.note: 逛 is fourth-tone guàng. this lesson uses 去逛逛 for going to look around a night market.
逛.memory: Write the seven-stroke 狂 body first, then finish with the three-stroke movement component 辶 wrapping along the lower-left.

parts.label: 狂
parts.name: inner component
parts.description: The first seven strokes form 狂, the compact inner body of 逛.

parts.label: 辶
parts.name: movement component
parts.description: The final three strokes form 辶 and sweep around the lower-left of the inner body.

逛.partOrderLabel: inner 狂, then wrapping 辶

u29-calendar-date.title: Say a month and date
u29-calendar-date.pattern: Number + 月 + Number + 號 / 日
u29-calendar-date.explanation: A month is formed with a number plus 月. A spoken day of the month commonly uses a number plus 號; 日 is also used as a written date form. The whole date functions as a Time-When expression and therefore comes before the action.

examples.text: 我女朋友九月三十號要來看我。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ nǚpéngyou jiǔyuè sānshí hào yào lái kàn wǒ.
examples.meaning: My girlfriend is coming to see me on September 30.
I return to my country on September 30.

u29-calendar-date.remember: Month first, then day: 九月三十號. Put the complete date before the action.

u29-yaoshi-jiu.title: Condition and consequence with 要是…就…
u29-yaoshi-jiu.pattern: 要是 + Condition，(Subject) + 就 + Consequence / Subject + 要是 + Condition，Subject + 就 + Consequence
u29-yaoshi-jiu.explanation: 要是 introduces the condition. 就 stands at the beginning of the predicate in the consequence clause. The subject can come before 要是 or after it. The condition or consequence may be negative; keep 就 in the consequence clause.

examples.text: 要是我有空，我就跟你一起去。
examples.pinyin: Yàoshi wǒ yǒu kòng, wǒ jiù gēn nǐ yìqǐ qù.
examples.meaning: If I am free, then I will go with you.

examples.text: 你要是沒空，我們就不去夜市。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ yàoshi méi kòng, wǒmen jiù bú qù yèshì.
examples.meaning: If you are not free, then we will not go to the night market.

u29-yaoshi-jiu.remember: 要是 marks the if-clause; 就 marks what follows from it.

u29-date.text: 我女朋友九月三十號要來看我。
u29-date.pinyin: Wǒ nǚpéngyou jiǔyuè sānshí hào yào lái kàn wǒ.
u29-date.meaning: My girlfriend is coming to see me on September 30.
u29-date.note: 九月三十號 is a complete Time-When expression. this lesson also gives 女 + person noun as female-/girl- (for example 女學生); 女朋友 is the fixed word girlfriend.

u29-return-date.meaning: I return to my country on September 30.
u29-return-date.note: The date comes before 回國.

u29-still.note: 還 means still in this sentence.

u29-additional.meaning: There are also tea houses here.
u29-additional.note: 還 can also add another item: also / in addition.

u29-maokong.meaning: The scenery in Maokong is beautiful.
u29-maokong.note: 貓空 is the Taipei place name used in this visit context.

u29-if-free.text: 要是我有空，我就跟你一起去。
u29-if-free.pinyin: Yàoshi wǒ yǒu kòng, wǒ jiù gēn nǐ yìqǐ qù.
u29-if-free.meaning: If I am free, then I will go with you.
u29-if-free.note: 要是 presents the condition and 就 presents the consequence.

u29-if-not-free.text: 你要是沒空，我們就不去夜市。
u29-if-not-free.pinyin: Nǐ yàoshi méi kòng, wǒmen jiù bú qù yèshì.
u29-if-not-free.meaning: If you are not free, then we will not go to the night market.
u29-if-not-free.note: The condition is negative, and 就 still introduces the consequence.

u29-fruit.text: 她來的時候，我們一起吃水果。
u29-fruit.pinyin: Tā lái de shíhou, wǒmen yìqǐ chī shuǐguǒ.
u29-fruit.meaning: When she comes, we will eat fruit together.
u29-fruit.note: 水果 begins the fruit topic while 的時候 deliberately recycles the earlier time-setting pattern.

u29-yellow-fruit.pinyin: Zhèlǐ hái yǒu huángsè de shuǐguǒ.
u29-yellow-fruit.meaning: There is also yellow fruit here.
u29-yellow-fruit.note: 還有 adds another item; 黃色的 modifies 水果.

u29-give-piece.text: 在貓空，我給你一塊水果。
u29-give-piece.pinyin: Zài Māokōng, wǒ gěi nǐ yí kuài shuǐguǒ.
u29-give-piece.meaning: At Maokong, I’ll give you a piece of fruit.
u29-give-piece.note: 給 + person + thing means give someone something. 塊 also counts pieces of food: 一塊水果 is one piece of fruit. This extends the price use of 塊 you already know.

u29-fragrant.text: 要是水果很香，我就想吃。
u29-fragrant.pinyin: Yàoshi shuǐguǒ hěn xiāng, wǒ jiù xiǎng chī.
u29-fragrant.meaning: If the fruit smells fragrant, then I want to eat it.
u29-fragrant.note: 香 describes the smell; 要是 introduces the condition and 就 introduces the consequence.

u29-sweet.text: 要是水果不甜，我就不吃。
u29-sweet.pinyin: Yàoshi shuǐguǒ bù tián, wǒ jiù bù chī.
u29-sweet.meaning: If the fruit is not sweet, then I will not eat it.
u29-sweet.note: The condition is negative with 不甜; the consequence is also negative with 不吃.

u29-before-fruit.pinyin: Wǒ yǐqián bù xǐhuān chī shuǐguǒ.
u29-before-fruit.meaning: In the past, I didn’t like eating fruit.
u29-before-fruit.note: 以前 places the preference in an earlier time period.

u29-stroll.text: 夜市很有名，你們應該去逛逛。
u29-stroll.pinyin: Yèshì hěn yǒumíng, nǐmen yīnggāi qù guàngguang.
u29-stroll.meaning: Night markets are famous; you should go look around.
u29-stroll.note: This uses 逛 in the visit context without introducing the separately deferred 臺 character. Reduplication 逛逛 makes the activity light/casual here.
